usstates <- read.csv('data/usstates.csv')
library(ggplot2)

Research Question:

Does Mean Household Income and Percentage of Smoking Residents predict Obesity Rate across US States
model1 <- lm(Obese~HouseholdIncome + Smokers, usstates)
summary(model1)
## 
## Call:
## lm(formula = Obese ~ HouseholdIncome + Smokers, data = usstates)
## 
## Residuals:
##    Min     1Q Median     3Q    Max 
## -5.814 -1.460  0.033  1.132  4.261 
## 
## Coefficients:
##                 Estimate Std. Error t value Pr(>|t|)    
## (Intercept)     28.09965    4.56292   6.158 1.55e-07 ***
## HouseholdIncome -0.12528    0.04716  -2.657   0.0107 *  
## Smokers          0.61059    0.12868   4.745 1.98e-05 ***
## ---
## Signif. codes:  0 '***' 0.001 '**' 0.01 '*' 0.05 '.' 0.1 ' ' 1
## 
## Residual standard error: 2.304 on 47 degrees of freedom
## Multiple R-squared:  0.6505, Adjusted R-squared:  0.6356 
## F-statistic: 43.74 on 2 and 47 DF,  p-value: 1.866e-11
ggplot(usstates, aes(HouseholdIncome, Obese)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = F, color = "steelblue") +
  labs(x = "Mean Household Income (in $1000)", y = "Obesity Rate")

ggplot(usstates, aes(Smokers, Obese)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = F, color = "steelblue")

  labs(x = "Smoking Rate", y = "Obesity Rate")
## $x
## [1] "Smoking Rate"
## 
## $y
## [1] "Obesity Rate"
## 
## attr(,"class")
## [1] "labels"
ggplot(usstates, aes(HouseholdIncome, Obese, color = Smokers)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = F, color = "gray") +
  scale_color_gradient(low = "yellow", high = "darkred") +
  labs(x = "Mean Household Income (in $1000)", y = "Obesity Rate")

plot(model1, 1:2)

confint(model1)
##                      2.5 %      97.5 %
## (Intercept)     18.9202483 37.27905944
## HouseholdIncome -0.2201457 -0.03041529
## Smokers          0.3517204  0.86946815
library(car)
vif(model1)
## HouseholdIncome         Smokers 
##         1.87035         1.87035
